title: [Audit] 🔐 Identity & Access
description: Who authenticated, how, from where, and what failed. Resolves the numeric user.name into real identities.

config.description: All distinct identities, human and machine.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS `Identities` = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor)

config.description: Distinct human identities by email address.
Distinct API key ids seen authenticating in range, and how many names they go by. A re-issued key keeps its name under a new id, so there can be fewer names than keys.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.api_key.id IS NOT NULL | STATS `API keys` = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.api_key.id), names = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.api_key.name) | EVAL detail = CONCAT("under ", TO_STRING(names), CASE(names == 1, " name", " names")) | KEEP `API keys`, detail

config.description: Events authenticated through the cloud-saml-kibana SAML realm — interactive human sign-in.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana" | STATS `SSO events` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Failed sign-ins (authentication_failed, realm_authentication_failed, anonymous_access_denied) plus requests refused or failed after sign-in (access_denied and any failed outcome). The line under the number splits the two: a denial is an authenticated identity hitting a permission wall, not someone guessing credentials. Same predicate as the Failed or denied access table, so the two always agree.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" | STATS `Failed or denied` = COUNT(*), signin = COUNT(*) WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") | EVAL detail = CONCAT(TO_STRING(signin), " failed sign-ins · ", TO_STRING(`Failed or denied` - signin), " denied") | KEEP `Failed or denied`, detail

config.description: Distinct Kibana browser sessions observed in range.

config.title: Authentication method over time
config.description: Elasticsearch requests per interval by how they presented credentials: API key, token (SSO browser sessions and service accounts) or realm (username and password). Log scale, one line per credential type, so a type carrying a fraction of a percent of the traffic is as readable as the bulk. A shift in this mix is worth explaining.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.authentication.type IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), attributes.authentication.type | EVAL auth = CASE(attributes.authentication.type == "api_key", "API key", attributes.authentication.type == "token", "Token", attributes.authentication.type == "realm", "Realm", attributes.authentication.type == "anonymous", "Anonymous", attributes.authentication.type == "internal", "Internal", attributes.authentication.type)

config.title: Credential type by identity
config.description: Which credential type each of the 12 busiest identities presents; the stronger the colour, the more events. Humans should authenticate by token (SSO); service identities by API key. Only Elasticsearch requests record a credential type, so identities seen only in Kibana or only anonymously are counted in Identities above but are not on this chart. A Cloud API key with no name is shown by its id.

config.title: Identity origin
config.description: Traffic split by the email on the event: Elastic (@elastic.co), Tenant (any other address), or Machine (no email: service accounts, Cloud API keys, internal users and anonymous requests). An Elasticsearch API key carries its creator's email, so traffic from a key a person created counts under that person's origin.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY attributes.user.email | EVAL actor_org = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NULL, "machine", attributes.user.email LIKE "*@elastic.co", "Elastic", "tenant") | STATS events = SUM(events) BY actor_org | EVAL origin = CASE(actor_org == "machine", "Machine", actor_org == "tenant", "Tenant", actor_org)

config.title: Authentication realm
config.description: Which security realm authenticated the request. SAML SSO is interactive human sign-in (cloud-saml-kibana); Elasticsearch API key (_es_api_key) and Cloud API key (_cloud_api_key) are programmatic; Service account is Elastic's own components (_service_account). Any other realm is shown by its name.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.domain IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY attributes.user.domain | EVAL realm = CASE(attributes.user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana", "SAML SSO", attributes.user.domain == "_es_api_key", "Elasticsearch API key", attributes.user.domain == "_cloud_api_key", "Cloud API key", STARTS_WITH(attributes.user.domain, "_service_account"), "Service account", STARTS_WITH(attributes.user.domain, "_"), "Other internal", attributes.user.domain) | STATS events = SUM(events) BY realm

config.title: Busiest API keys
config.description: The busiest API keys, one row per key id, with the owner (the creator's email, stamped on keys a person created; a Cloud API key records none), request volume and how many distinct client IPs used it. A key used from many IPs is worth investigating. A re-issued key keeps its name under a new id, so a name can appear twice. The full list, with first and last use, is API key inventory below.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.api_key.name IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip) BY api_key = attributes.api_key.name, key_id = attributes.api_key.id, owner = attributes.user.email | EVAL owner = COALESCE(owner, "none recorded") | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 9

config.title: Human identity footprint
config.description: People by email, busiest first, with their first and last appearance in the selected range and how many client IPs they came from. Click an email to pin that person across the suite.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip) BY attributes.user.email | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Failed or denied access
config.description: Failed sign-ins and refused requests grouped by identity, action and source IP, most frequent first. authentication_failed, realm_authentication_failed and anonymous_access_denied are failed sign-ins; access_denied is an authenticated identity refused an action. Empty is good.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, action = attributes.event.action, ip = client.ip | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = SUM(events), last_seen = MAX(last_seen) BY actor, action, ip | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Failed sign-ins and denied access
config.description: Every failed sign-in and refused request, newest first. Kind separates a failed sign-in from a denial after sign-in.

config.title: API key inventory
config.description: Every API key id seen in range, busiest first, with owner, volume, IP spread, indices touched and first and last use.

config.title: Identity first and last seen
config.description: Every identity with its first and last appearance within the selected time range, its event count, and how many IPs, countries and actions it used. Newest first appearance on top. Widen the time range to tell a brand-new identity from one that was simply quiet. Noise gate applied, so counts run lower than on the panels above.
